text: Your iPhone screen is a sea of apps. You drag a few into a new folder, aiming for perfect organization. You tap the default title, ready to rename it custom.
But then, a wall. You can't type anything new. The tiny input box only allows a few characters. Your custom name simply doesn't fit the space.
You try everything: long press, settings, searching online. Is it a bug? A hidden feature? You assume it's an oversight, or you are missing a trick.
The truth is, it’s intentional. Apple decided folder names should be short and descriptive: one word. This design choice guides users to a standard, clean aesthetic.
The cost? You lose customization, but gain a universally understood interface. Apple optimizes for the average user experience, even if it limits power users.
Now, you organize your apps, but you see the invisible hand. That short, unchangeable folder name isn’t a bug; it’s a deliberate rule, shaping your world.
